Define an analytic constraint system (e.g., a set of linear or polynomial constraints on function values) with varying sample count w. Sweep hidden layer width N_c to find the minimum width achieving zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraints. Record N_c(w) and assess whether it plateaus (rigid) or diverges (fat).

Create a Python script to test the Interpolation Threshold Hypothesis. The script will: (1) Define a set of analytical constraints (e.g., linear equations, polynomial evaluations) to form the "analytical constraints" mentioned in the hypothesis; (2) Implement a small feedforward network (single hidden layer) with variable width N; (3) For increasing numbers of constraints w, train the network to satisfy these constraints (training error <= 1e-3); (4) Evaluate the maximum absolute error on a held-out set of constraints (leave-one-out or separate validation set); (5) Record the minimum width N_c(w) required to achieve "zero violation" (max error <= 1e-3) on the held-out set; (6) Plot N_c(w) vs w to determine if the solution space is "rigid" (N_c plateaus at small value) or "fat" (N_c grows or is unattainable). We will use a simple function like sin(x) or a polynomial as the target function to generate constraints.
